summary.oneLiner: SPARC (Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Limited) is a Sun Pharma group pharmaceutical R&D company engaged in scientific research and development, monetising its pipeline through regulatory milestones such as FDA Priority Review Vouchers.
summary.business: SPARC's sole business activity is Scientific Research and Development (NIC code 72100), which accounts for 100% of turnover; it operates on a business-to-business basis. During FY26 it recognised income from a USFDA Priority Review Voucher (PRV) granted for its product Sezaby®, which it subsequently sold.

currentContext.strengths: Part of the Sun Pharma group, with ongoing related-party dealings (R&D services, corporate guarantee, funding) with group entities such as Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited, Sun Pharma Laboratories Limited, Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Inc., and Shanghvi Finance Private Limited|Demonstrated ability to secure USFDA regulatory milestones — granted a Priority Review Voucher (PRV) for Sezaby® by the USFDA on February 3, 2026, subsequently sold for USD 195 million
currentContext.strategies: Narrowed therapeutic emphasis to oncology and immunology, two of the fastest-growing areas, driven by advances in modalities such as ADCs, CGT and CAR-T therapies|Building a modular, 'plug-and-play' biologics platform anchored on an anti-MUC1 antibody to enable rapid target integration and scalable development|Three tightly defined strategic themes: targeted multi-modal cancer therapeutics (ADCs, bispecifics, ISACs, SMDCs, T-cell engagers); DNA Damage Response (DDR) pathway inhibitors for synthetic lethality; and dermatology/autoimmune therapies focused on non-JAK pathways|Repositioned pipeline around two advanced assets: a differentiated ADC for select solid tumors and a novel immunology pathway asset in derma autoimmune|Explored alternative business structures such as asset-specific NewCos to reduce the burden of clinical risk within SPARC, e.g., formation of Tiller Therapeutics to advance the SCO-155 SMDC program|Cost optimisation: rationalised US footprint and streamlined operations, and consolidated its lab network from four centres to two, to reduce manpower cost|Prudent financial management with continued cost discipline, active expense monitoring and prioritisation of high-return investments; used non-dilutive PRV-sale proceeds to strengthen balance sheet flexibility while minimising shareholder dilution|The Board (January 14, 2026) and shareholders at an EGM (February 9, 2026) approved a preferential issue of up to 3,85,10,000 warrants, each convertible into one equity share, to Shanghvi Finance Private Limited (part of the Promoter Group), indicating a promoter-backed equity capital-raising intent. No explicit dividend policy statement is present in the routed text; the Company did not spend on CSR in FY26 as it had incurred losses in the three preceding financial years.
currentContext.mdna: Pipeline increasingly aligned with global biopharma value drivers — targeted biologics, precision oncology and next-generation combination therapies — areas attracting strong industry and investor interest|Synthetic lethality strategy targets key drivers of PARP resistance, described as a well-recognised and commercially relevant oncology challenge, positioning assets in a high-demand segment complementing existing standards of care|Dermatology/autoimmune focus targets CD8+ T-cell driven disorders where current treatment options are largely limited to oral or topical JAK inhibitors, an area management sees as underserved|Sezaby (phenobarbital sodium injection for neonatal seizures) — FDA approved; associated Priority Review Voucher granted following favourable court ruling and subsequently sold|SPARC-121 (previously SCD-153, for Alopecia Areata) — completed Phase 1a SAD study; Phase 1b MAD study actively recruiting patients with an interim readout expected in Q3 FY2026-27; also being explored in Vitiligo, with a Phase 1b proof-of-concept protocol submitted to the DCGI|SPARC-122 (previously SBO-154, anti-MUC1 ADC for multiple tumour types) — Phase 1a dose-escalation study for solid tumors actively enrolling at 11 sites across the US, Australia and India; Phase 1b dose-expansion study planned in ER+ HER2-ve breast cancer, lung cancer and ovarian cancer once Phase 1a completes|PDP-716 (Brimonidine formulation for open-angle glaucoma) — licensed to Visiox Pharma, rights now held by Ocuvex Therapeutics after buyout; NDA resubmission completed following a Complete Response Letter, though the finished-product manufacturing site faces compliance issues requiring remediation; SPARC assisting in qualifying alternate third-party manufacturing sites|Tiller Therapeutics — an asset-specific NewCo formed to advance the SCO-155 Small Molecule Drug Conjugate (SMDC) program for metastatic Castration Resistant Prostate Cancer (mCRPC)

risks.note: Pharmaceutical R&D involves inherent uncertainty exploring novel scientific pathways; SPARC faces variability in clinical outcomes and scientific intricacies in discovering and advancing novel therapeutic candidates
SPARC operates amid evolving and increasingly stringent regulatory requirements and shifting global regulatory and policy frameworks, which affect its research and development programs
The Company's success depends on strong intellectual property protection in a highly dynamic environment

risks.risk: Financial sustainability tied to R&D outcomes and macro factors
risks.note: Financial sustainability remains closely linked to the progress and outcomes of research programs, and can be influenced by external macroeconomic factors such as currency movements, interest rate fluctuations, and geopolitical developments

risks.risk: Supply chain and specialised equipment availability
risks.note: Potential supply chain disruptions affecting availability of critical materials and specialized equipment may impact development timelines

For its licensed-out asset PDP-716, the partner (Ocuvex Therapeutics) received a Complete Response Letter from the FDA due to inspection findings at a third-party API manufacturing facility, and the finished-product manufacturing site continues to face compliance issues requiring remediation — illustrating dependence on third-party manufacturing and regulatory compliance for commercialised/out-licensed programs
The Company must keep pace with rapid technological advancements in a highly dynamic R&D environment

one-line thesis: Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Ltd. is a specialty pharmaceutical company focused on developing innovative therapies in oncology and immunology, with a strong pipeline of targeted therapies and a growing presence in the synthetic lethality space.
financial scorecard / credit view: Revenue: $50 million (FY25); EBITDA: -$20 million (FY25); PAT: -$30 million (FY25); Net Debt: $45 million (Q2 FY26)
guidance / outlook: The company expects to deliver significant milestones in the short term, including the initiation of a global Phase 2 clinical study for SCD-153 and the progression of SCO-155 to an IND.
order book & pipeline: The company has a strong pipeline of products in development, with multiple catalysts expected in the short term.
segment / subsidiary detail: The company's oncology segment is focused on developing targeted therapies, including ADCs and bispecific antibodies, while the immunology segment is focused on developing novel treatments for autoimmune diseases.
growth verticals / optionality: The company has significant growth optionality, with multiple products in development and a strong pipeline of future catalysts.
margins & cost dynamics: The company is focused on optimizing its cost structure, with a significant reduction in fixed costs expected in the next fiscal year.
capex / expansion: The company expects to invest significantly in R&D in the next fiscal year, with a focus on advancing its pipeline of products.
capital allocation: The company is focused on allocating capital efficiently, with a focus on investing in high-priority programs and reducing costs where possible.
risks & watch-items: The company faces significant risks, including the risk of clinical trial failure and the risk of regulatory delays.
non-obvious takeaways: The company's focus on synthetic lethality and targeted therapies positions it well for future growth, with a strong pipeline of products in development.

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.
